note: New Caledonia has its own labour code (Code du travail de Nouvelle-Calédonie, CTNC, the DTE's consolidation of 12 June 2026) and, since 2013, its own competence in civil law. Majority: null. The Code civil as it applies in New Caledonia wasn't read: juridoc.gouv.nc's codes base is a frameset whose pages gave no list of codes to this client (2026-10-31), and France's own pages speak for the Code civil as the State keeps it, which isn't New Caledonia's text since the transfer. Work: 16. CTNC Lp. 251-1: children may not be employed in any capacity before being freed of compulsory schooling, which the DTE's page says lasts to 16. Lp. 251-2 lets those over 14 do light work in school holidays (rest of at least half of each holiday, with the labour inspectorate's prior agreement; R. 251-1: the employer declares the hire 15 days before, the inspector has eight days to object) and school-linked placements: not held. Performers: barred, the reading being that the CTNC has no exception for young performers, unlike the French Code du travail (its chapter on artists, Lp. 615-1 ff., is about portage salarial): under 14 none may be employed, and 14 to 16 only in the holiday light work above. Lp. 253-1 bars night work under 18 with exceptional derogations for commerce and entertainment: not held. Service: none. Conscription has been suspended since 1997; the Ministère des Armées' page for the new service national says it is voluntary and selective with no compulsory character, open to those living in mainland France or overseas, 18 to 25. The recensement citoyen from 16 and the journée défense et citoyenneté remain (Service Public F870), not held.
